inputs.statement: n=λ+1>0 and card(I)=n. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V; e_0=v. For every integer m≥0, h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v; for m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v. The vectors y^m v vanish for m>λ. The action matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power matrix coefficients are integers.

ι_R:M_R→V is injective, its image spans V over ℂ, and M_R is free of rank n over R. Under this embedding M_R is stable under all X_r,Y_r (r≥0). For every integer t with 0≤t≤λ, t! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M and give its induced Chevalley action after tensoring.

output.statement: n>0. All the R-submodules Jcoord_i (i∈I) equal J. J is nonzero and finitely generated over R. Inside V one has M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i: explicitly every element of M_R has a unique expression ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i with c_i∈J, and every such finite sum belongs to M_R. Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map T→ℂ, q⊗c↦qc, is injective, T is finite dimensional over ℚ and dim_ℚ T=1. For every nonzero a∈J and every c∈J there exists q∈ℚ with c=qa.

locals.declaration: Put T=ℚ⊗_R J with the usual ℚ-vector space structure.
Define μ(q⊗c)=qc by the balanced bilinear multiplication map.
Define Φ on simple tensors by Φ(q⊗∑c_i e_i)=(q⊗c_i)_i using the coordinate decomposition F001.

argument.text: Use the embedding of N002. E_ii maps M_R onto Jcoord_i e_i, because it extracts the i-th coordinate on the N001 basis. For i,j∈I and c∈Jcoord_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i belongs to M_R by N002, so c∈Jcoord_i. Interchanging i,j proves equality. N001 gives 0∈I and e_0=v, hence the common module is J. The projection E_00 of a finite R-basis of M_R (N002) gives finitely many generators of J e_0; since e_0≠0, their coefficients generate J. If J were zero every projection E_ii would vanish on M_R, and their sum is Id_V, so M_R would be zero. This contradicts its complex span V and n>0 from N001. Finally, coordinate projections show each element of M_R has coordinates in J; conversely each sum ∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J belongs to M_R. Uniqueness is complex independence of e. Thus M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

produces.statement: n>0; Jcoord_i=J for all i∈I; J is nonzero and finitely generated over R; M_R consists exactly of the sums ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i with c_i∈J and these coordinates are unique.

argument.text: Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map μ:T→ℂ is defined on simple tensors by μ(q⊗c)=qc. It is well-defined by additivity and R-balancing. Every tensor is a finite sum of simple tensors. Write its finitely many rational first factors over a common nonzero integer denominator d; balancing integer numerators into J writes the tensor as (1/d)⊗c for one c∈J. If its image in ℂ is zero, c/d=0, so c=0 and the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. If c_1,…,c_s is a finite R-generating family of J from F001, then 1⊗c_1,…,1⊗c_s spans T over ℚ by tensor bilinearity. In particular T is finitely generated as a ℚ-module, that is finite dimensional.

produces.statement: T=ℚ⊗_R J is a finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space, and μ:T→ℂ, μ(q⊗c)=qc, is injective.

argument.text: The coordinate isomorphism in F001 induces an explicit ℚ-linear equivalence Φ:ℚ⊗_R M_R→∏_{i∈I}T: on q⊗∑c_i e_i it gives (q⊗c_i)_{i∈I}. For clarity, define its inverse by summing the maps T→ℚ⊗_R M_R induced by c↦c e_i: a tuple (q_i⊗c_i)_i maps to ∑_i q_i⊗(c_i e_i), extended additively in each entry. Both maps are defined by balanced bilinear maps. On simple tensors their composites are identities, by uniqueness of the coordinates and finite distributivity; simple tensors generate, so these checks prove both inverse identities. This supplies the rationalized direct-sum identification, not just a count.

produces.statement: There is a ℚ-linear equivalence Φ:ℚ⊗_R M_R≃∏_{i∈I}T sending q⊗∑c_i e_i to (q⊗c_i)_{i∈I}.

argument.text: Put r=dim_ℚ T. N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R indexed by I. Applying M001 with A=R and B=ℚ to this basis gives a ℚ-basis of ℚ⊗_R M_R indexed by I; M002 over ℚ therefore gives its dimension as card(I)=n, using N001. Apply M007 with A=ℚ to T to obtain freeness. The finite generation in F002 and this freeness verify the module premises of M004. Thus M004 with the constant family T over I gives dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}T)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. M005 applied to Φ from F003 equates these dimensions: n=nr. Because n>0, r=1.

For any nonzero a∈J, injectivity of μ in F002 gives 1⊗a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent over ℚ: a scalar annihilating a nonzero vector in a vector space over a field is zero. Apply M003 with A=ℚ, ambient space T, the singleton index type and this singleton family. F004 gives the required dimension 1, so every 1⊗c with c∈J is q(1⊗a) for some q∈ℚ. Applying μ gives c=qa. Together with F001–F004 this proves the stated coordinate decomposition, injectivity, and rational rank-one conclusion.
